speaker: john_heminges
text: It is done. The yard is out.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I spoke, and then I sat two hours in that parlour. It is still cold.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: You wore it well enough. The old man came back when he was wanted.

speaker: will_kemp
text: And the rest of us worked, while you had a chair. By my hose, I call that a part.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Call it what you like, Will. The chair was not a kindness.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Thou art in, at any rate. Leave the cold in the parlour.

speaker: will_kemp
text: I have a better cold to give you. The Admiral's men. Yesterday, at the Rose, they played the second Tamburlaine, and by candle-time they were before the Queen at Greenwich.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Both in a day. That is a company with a horse, or a lie.

speaker: john_heminges
text: It is the talk. I have not seen their book.

speaker: will_kemp
text: You do not need their book. You need Alleyn. Stand aside.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Holla, ye pampered jades of Asia!

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You have made them quiet, Will, and you were mocking.

speaker: john_heminges
text: They will be paid as slowly as we are.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: One company at court on New Year's Day, the other on St Stephen's. She is keeping two dogs and feeding neither.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Holla, ye pampered jades of Asia!

speaker: will_kemp
text: Richard. That was my chariot you have struck, and almost my head.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: The stool was enough. You did not need a second roar.

speaker: will_kemp
text: The second roar is the play. Alleyn would have had three.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: Alleyn is at Greenwich, and we are in a parlour that smells of the yard. I know which I can spend.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Spend nothing on a guess. Their money is as slow as ours, and ours is not in the hand.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Twenty pounds, not yet had. It is in my book as expected. It is not mine to fetch, John.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Expected is a fine word, i' faith, for a purse that stays at court.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Thou hast sheets under thine arm. Is that the answer to Alleyn?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is Berowne. He stays in the sheets. I am not reading him out in a tiring-room.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Then keep him. I asked nothing of the page.

speaker: thomas_pope
text: A page will not out-shout a man on a hamper. You have just heard the proof.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Let the page alone. The afternoon is done, and Monday is another Errors. Will, you are the old man again.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I know it, John. I will sit the middle again, and I will not ask the room to pity the chair.

speaker: will_kemp
text: Pity is not my line. The hamper is. Marry, if the Queen wants a chariot she may send for Alleyn, and we will send her a comedy when we have one.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: When thou hast one. Not tonight.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Not tonight.
